command: uv run python -m eval.stress_battery --source <corpus data> --scratch <dir> --out <record> --queries <16 titles> --tokenizer legacy --passes 5 --fresh 3 --fresh-qids L0,L11,L23 --path-qids L0,L6,L11,L17,L23 --runs 3

corpus.tokenizer: LEGACY (the file predates the recorded identity)

queries.titles: 16: ten from the query set of an earlier, unpublished study of the stores (L0..L25, their places in it) and six drawn independently (S0..S5); texts not recorded

conditions.load: the one-minute load average, read beside every timing

not_run.stratum: not run: a sentence admitting the dialogue stratum loads every row of it with its vector (`all_rows(DIALOGUE_READ)`, core/sentence/universe.py) and builds dense n by n matrices over the items; the corpus instance's stage-1 record (docs/experiments/corpus-stage1-2026-11-07.md) has 4.3 to 4.7 GB at 10,000 items, and the whole corpus would need tens of GB. It belongs to a bounded universe, not to this battery
not_run.cut: not run: the test that a commit's cut holds a citation edge reads every edge of the commit (`ReferenceEdgeStore.for_commit`, from core/sentence/universe.py); it needs a citation store, and an instance without one, as the corpus instance is, has no edge for it to read
not_run.mask: not run: the pending mask of a sentence's nodes (core/sentence/universe.py) builds the set of pending items again for each node; it is empty when nothing is pending, as on the corpus instance, where `derive.pending` finds 0 items

code.label: branch-f1a1f49c
code.same_tree_as: b37d02e9: the same tree, the commit made again when the subject of an earlier commit was reworded

migration.note: each the first open of a fresh clone by the branch's code, with the one-minute load read when its part or process began (in a landing process the ledger was opened after the lexical index, two minutes later)

earlier_runs.note: the record's first version: run 1 main at f969904e, run 2 the branch at 2bedbcf1, run 3 the keyword and ledger parts at f1a1f49c (the tree of b37d02e9); three warm passes a query; no prepared source, so the branch's parts ran on a file its first open had just read whole (the migration)
